(1) cross lingual methods are competitive with monolingual approaches, and that (2) synthetic treebanking is the key to successful cross lingual dependency treebanking.

(a) cross lingual dependency treebanking is a viable method to create treebanks for languages that do not have any dependency treebank available, (b) the quality of the source treebank is a crucial factor for success, (c) the accuracy of the POS tagger used for projection is also important for the success, (d) machine translation can be used to improve the quality of the treebank, and (e) cross lingual treebanking is not a panacea

cross lingual dependency parsers can achieve state of the art results for under resourced languages, that synthetic treebanks can be used for this purpose, that the quality of synthetic treebanks can vary significantly, and that parsing accuracy is sensitive to the quality of the POS tagger used.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question how to best exploit the resources available for the source and target languages to build a dependency parser for the latter.
the question how we can make use of the available resources to build a dependency parser for a language with no treebank available.
making use of the wealth of existing treebanks in order to build models for parsing under resourced languages, and to make the best of the available data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cross lingual dependency treebanking and parsing can provide a viable and efficient alternative to traditional approaches for languages for which no or only limited treebanks are available.
synthetic treebanking is a very promising technique that is likely to become the dominant approach for cross lingual dependency tree parsing.

cross lingual dependency parsers are now competitive with the best monolingual dependency parsers for the source languages, and that they are a viable alternative for parsing the languages that lack treebanks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cross lingual parsing can be used to build dependency parsers for languages for which no dependency treebanks exist.
the combination of synthetic treebanking with machine translation and annotation projection provides a very promising and practical method for cross lingual dependency analysis.
cross lingual dependency parsers can be competitive with the state of the art for under resourced languages if they are based on synthetic treebanks.
The main takeaway from our work is that

synthetic treebanking is a promising approach for cross lingual parsing, and that it is possible to obtain good quality dependency parses of languages for which no resource exists, by combining various methods that make up the synthetic treebanking pipeline.
synthetic treebanks, while being a valuable resource in cross lingual parsing, are not a replacement for real treebanks.

synthetic treebanking is a promising technique for cross lingual parsing, but the results are not always as good as one might hope for, and that the success of cross lingual parsing methods is very dependent on the quality of the source treebank and the source to target language alignment.
